pnl_attribution_test_frtb_pat.text: `residual_pnl_unexplained` takes one period's actual P&L and a set of explained components, then returns the leftover: actual P&L minus the sum of those components. It also gives the ratio of explained to actual, so it answers "how much of this period's P&L did my explained pieces fail to capture?" `pnl_attribution_test_frtb_pat` works on two daily series, risk-theoretical P&L (`risk_theoretical_pnl`) and hypothetical P&L (`hypothetical_pnl`). It measures their Spearman rank correlation and the ratio of their standard deviations, then assigns a Basel traffic-light zone. It answers "does the risk model's P&L track full-revaluation P&L well enough to pass the FRTB test?" So the first is a single-period decomposition that reconstructs actual P&L exactly, while the second is a pass/fail-style assessment of model quality over a series. A large residual can point to model incompleteness, which is the kind of concern the FRTB test looks at.

explain.text: `residual_pnl_unexplained` calculates the unexplained (residual) P&L for a period. It subtracts the sum of your explained P&L components (`explained_components`) from the observed, hypothetical P&L (`actual_pnl`). The residual plus the explained components reconstructs the actual P&L exactly. The formula also defines a ratio of explained components to actual P&L. A large residual relative to actual P&L flags model incompleteness, which is an FRTB PAT concern.

when.text:
`residual_pnl_unexplained` fits when you need to see how much of a period's P&L your explained components fail to capture.

- You have an observed (hypothetical) P&L and a set of explained components, such as Greeks or other attribution pieces, and want the leftover: actual P&L minus the sum of the components.
- You want a check that the residual plus the explained components reconstructs actual P&L exactly.
- You want to see whether the residual is large relative to actual P&L, which flags model incompleteness. This is an FRTB PAT concern.
- You want the ratio of explained components to actual P&L as a quick measure of how much your model explains.

If you need the formal FRTB test itself, `pnl_attribution_test_frtb_pat` is listed as the FRTB P&L Attribution Test (PAT), using a Spearman correlation and ratio test.
